purpose: Calcium carbonate is used to relieve heartburn, acid indigestion, and upset stomach. It is also taken as a calcium supplement to help keep your bones and teeth strong. Doctors sometimes recommend it to people who do not get enough calcium from their diet.
how_it_works: When you take it for heartburn, calcium carbonate quickly neutralizes the extra acid in your stomach, which is what causes that burning feeling. Think of it like baking soda putting out a small fire — it calms the acid down fast. When used as a supplement, it provides your body with calcium, which your bones and muscles need to stay healthy and strong.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are constipation, gas, and bloating. Some people notice a chalky taste in their mouth. Taking too much can cause nausea or stomach upset.
warnings: Do not take more than the recommended dose, as too much calcium can cause a condition called hypercalcemia, which means too much calcium in your blood — this can cause confusion, muscle weakness, and kidney problems. Let your doctor know if you have kidney disease or kidney stones before taking this. Calcium carbonate can also interfere with how your body absorbs certain other medications, so take other medicines at least 1 to 2 hours apart from this one.
typical_dosing: For heartburn in adults, the usual dose is 500 to 1000 mg (1 to 2 regular Tums tablets) as needed, up to a few times a day. For a calcium supplement, most adults take 500 to 1200 mg per day in divided doses, usually with meals since food helps your body absorb it better. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions for your situation.
